newsitem.title: ITALY: New Alitalia unit to coordinate Malpensa move.
newsitem.headline: New Alitalia unit to coordinate Malpensa move.

text.p: Alitalia said it will establish an operations unit in Milan during April to coordinate flight operations and crew schedules, ahead of the move to Milan's Malpensa airport from the city's other airport at Linate.

Alitalia Chief Operating Officer Domenico Cempella made the announcement at a meeting on Monday of key local authority, airline and union representatives to study the transfer of operations to Malpensa from Linate.
The new unit will help to coordinate the shift of Alitalia activities to Malpensa in time for the opening of the airline's second operational hub at that airport on January 1, 1998, Cempella said.
Separately the meeting also agreed to set up four working groups to review potential problems associated with the move to Malpensa from Linate, air industry sources said.
The working groups will cover airport operational activities, staff transfers, employment aspects and the economic impact of the switch to Malpensa, the sources added
